newsitem.title: UK: IPE Jan Brent futures close up after brief rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE Jan Brent futures close up after brief rally.

text.p: IPE January Brent crude closed up on the day but off highs made in the last half hour of trading which were fueled by a short rally on NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.
January IPE Brent ended the day 13 cents firmer at $22.75 a barrel after prompt shorts tried to cover their positions and found sellers rare.
The February contract closed up nine cents at $22.22 a barrel.

"There was a brief rally led by a small bounce on the (NYMEX) heating oil which had led the market down earlier. At the time there were no sellers on the Brent. It's held some of the gains made then," one broker said.
NYMEX heating oil lost ground on Tuesday in a weak cash market with supplies seen as adequate while gasoline remained strong with New York spot market availabilities seen tight.
"Everyone is waiting for the API's and a bit nervous to go short ahead of tomorrow," he added.
Weekly U.S. stock statistics from the American Petroleum Institute were due to be released after markets close on Tuesday.
Brokers said there was no fresh market moving news and that the possibility of Iraq selling limited amounts of crude oil on the market in the near future was already factored into the price.
"The sentiment (about Iraq selling limited crude volumes) is pretty neutral," another commented.
Traders generally expected the ministers at the current OPEC meeting in Vienna to announce a rollover of the current production ceiling after several oil ministers at the meeting called for one.
"Everyone expects OPEC to rollover (production ceiling)," one crude oil trader said.
December gas oil closed earlier down $2 at $217 a tonne and was expected to open on Wednesday unchanged to slightly softer.
